messages.author: c0637b27e3cf6030
messages.subject: default physical activity threshold values
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to find a reference for the default values of light/moderate/vigorous physical activity thresholds used in GGIR. 

The defaults in the code are 

threshold.lig=40,
threshold.mod=100,
threshold.vig=400

and in the intro vignette they are the same except threshold.lig=30 instead of 40.

What populations were these defaults developed for? What populations do people normally use them for?

I don't see these thresholds listed in the Published Cutpoints vignette (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/CutPoints.html). I also looked through the GGIR manual and can't find a source of these. 

I apologize if this is documented and I simply missed it.

thank you!

-Lena Kushleyeva

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] default physical activity threshold values
parts:
Hi Lena,

Some of the thresholds were chosen because they were considered sufficient in one specific study I worked on at the time when I wrote the code. They are not intended to be a recommendation for all use cases.

Sometimes we may want to round or average multiple thresholds proposed in papers to avoid the impression of extreme precession. They are not much more than a crude way to segment behaviour in intensity levels.

Further, once a default argument value has been set it is common practise in software to never change the default unless there is convincing evidence that a different default is better. This to support reproducibility. We know that there is no universally applicable optimal threshold combination, by which any default is by definition flawed. I think each user will have to decide for themselves what thresholds to use.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
